did_you_know.text: Did you know? Shechem was chosen as the place where Rehoboam went to be crowned because all Israel had gathered there to make him king.
Did you know? Rehoboam first consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon, asking them how he should respond to the people.
Did you know? The elders advised Rehoboam to act humbly: to be “a servant to the people,” serve them, and speak kindly to them—and in this way he would gain their lasting loyalty.
Did you know? The young advisers used a vivid metaphor to express how the burden would be made heavier: “My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist.”
Did you know? After Rehoboam rejected the elders’ advice, the text explains that this was part of the fulfillment of the word of the LORD delivered to Jeroboam through Ahijah the Shilonite.

Did you know? After Rehoboam’s harsh response, Israel declared, “What share do we have in David?” In this way, they expressed their rejection of the house of David and the political division that followed.

Did you know? Jeroboam was made king over all Israel, while only the tribe of Judah remained loyal to the house of David; this verse explicitly states that Benjamin was not counted as part of the northern kingdom either.
Did you know? Although Rehoboam gathered 180,000 warriors to restore the kingdom, the prophet Shemaiah commanded them not to fight their brothers—and the people obeyed and returned home.
Did you know? Jeroboam set up two golden calves, one at Bethel and the other at Dan, and told the people that there was no need to go up to Jerusalem.
Did you know? Jeroboam established a festival in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at Bethel—a festival the text describes as one he had devised in his own heart.
